tasks.task: On the cohort screener, select the 18-29 and 30-44 age group filters, then also select the Black ethnicity filter.
tasks.expected: Exactly two respondents remain — WHS-1002 and WHS-1005. The two age picks widen the age side (OR), but adding Black narrows across dimensions (AND), so it is not the six respondents a match-any build would show.

tasks.task: Select only the Hispanic ethnicity filter on the cohort screener.
tasks.expected: Exactly WHS-1001 and WHS-1006 are listed, and no other respondents show.

tasks.task: On the cohort screener, select the Asian ethnicity filter, then click the clear-all control.
tasks.expected: After clear-all every one of the 8 seeded respondents is listed again and the matching readout returns to 8 of 8.

tasks.task: Fill out the health survey with valid answers, submit it, then open the cohort screener.
tasks.expected: The new submission appears in the screener as WHS-1009 alongside the 8 seeded respondents.

tasks.task: Fill out the health survey with valid answers and submit it.
tasks.expected: A confirmation message appears indicating the survey was submitted successfully.

tasks.task: On the Wellness Self-Check page, type 7 for sleep hours, 3 for exercise days, and 4 for stress.
tasks.expected: The score reads 6.6 / 10 with the 'Fair' label, and it appears as soon as the last field is filled — no submit button needed.

tasks.task: On the Wellness Self-Check page, type 8 for sleep hours, 7 for exercise days, and 10 for stress.
tasks.expected: The score reads 7.0 / 10 labeled 'Thriving' — the exact 7.0 boundary lands in Thriving, not Fair — and the stress nudge toward the full survey shows since stress is 7 or higher.

tasks.task: Type 7 for sleep and 3 for exercise, then type 15 into the stress field; afterwards change stress to 5.
tasks.expected: With 15 an out-of-range message shows and no score is displayed at all (no stale value); after changing stress to 5 the message clears and the score reads 6.3 / 10.

tasks.task: On the Wellness Self-Check page, enter 6 sleep hours, 2 exercise days, and 8 stress, then read the displayed score.
tasks.expected: The score is shown in the app-wide score style — one decimal followed by ' / 10' — reading 4.5 / 10.

tasks.task: On the cohort screener, select the 18-29 and 30-44 age group filters, then also select the Black ethnicity filter.
tasks.expected: Exactly two respondents remain — WHS-1002 and WHS-1005. The two age picks widen the age side (OR), but adding Black narrows across dimensions (AND), so it is not the six respondents a match-any build would show.

tasks.task: Start the survey, answer Section A's three questions (age group 30-44, ethnicity Hispanic, overall wellness 8), click Next, and in Section B choose Yes on the pregnancy question.
tasks.expected: Section B initially shows only the pregnancy question; choosing Yes reveals exactly two additional questions (number of pregnancies and most recent year).

tasks.task: On the survey wizard, click the 'Fill with sample answers' button.
tasks.expected: It jumps straight to the review step, which lists answers grouped by the three sections; the pregnancy answer shows as No and there are no entries for the two hidden pregnancy follow-up questions.

tasks.task: Open the survey and click Next on Section A without answering anything.
tasks.expected: Validation messages appear for the unanswered required questions and the wizard stays on Section A instead of advancing.

tasks.task: Click 'Fill with sample answers', submit from the review step, then open the cohort screener.
tasks.expected: A thank-you confirmation with the new ID WHS-1009 appears, and the screener now lists WHS-1009 along with the 8 seeded respondents.

tasks.task: On the Wellness Self-Check page, type 7 for sleep hours, 3 for exercise days, and 4 for stress.
tasks.expected: The score reads 6.6 / 10 with the 'Fair' label, and it appears as soon as the last field is filled — no submit button needed.

tasks.task: Open the cohort screener with no filters applied and read the needs-attention shortlist in the insights strip.
tasks.expected: It lists exactly WHS-1006, WHS-1003, then WHS-1001 in that order — the 6.4 three-way tie among WHS-1001, WHS-1004 and WHS-1007 resolves to the lowest ID, WHS-1001, not WHS-1004, which sits ahead of WHS-1001 in the roster order and is what a build with no tie-break logic would surface.

tasks.task: In the insights strip, click the toggle to view just the two most recent weeks.
tasks.expected: The average wellness reads 7.0 / 10 for the recent window (Weeks 3 and 4: WHS-1005, WHS-1006, WHS-1007, WHS-1008) — different from the all-time 6.7 / 10.

tasks.task: Select only the 60+ age group filter and look at the insights strip.
tasks.expected: The stats recompute to the single matching respondent WHS-1006 — average 4.8 / 10 and a shortlist showing just WHS-1006 — with no blank, broken, or padded entries.

tasks.task: In the screener, select the Black ethnicity filter and look at the insights strip.
tasks.expected: The average recomputes to 7.9 / 10 over the three matching Black respondents (WHS-1002, WHS-1005, WHS-1007).

tasks.task: Select only the Hispanic ethnicity filter on the cohort screener.
tasks.expected: Exactly WHS-1001 and WHS-1006 are listed, and no other respondents show.

tasks.task: Open the Follow-Up Queue page.
tasks.expected: The three seeded flags show in their stages — WHS-1006 Pending with the note 'score under 5', WHS-1003 Contacted with 'left voicemail', WHS-1004 Resolved with 'all good' — and each stage count reads 1.

tasks.task: On the Follow-Up Queue, advance WHS-1006 one stage.
tasks.expected: WHS-1006 moves from Pending to Contacted; the Pending stage now counts 0 and shows a non-blank empty state, and Contacted counts 2 (WHS-1003 and WHS-1006).

tasks.task: On the cohort screener, try to flag WHS-1003, which is already in the queue.
tasks.expected: A second flag is prevented — the flag control is disabled or clearly indicates WHS-1003 is already flagged — and no duplicate entry appears in the queue.

tasks.task: On the cohort screener, flag WHS-1001 and type 'check sleep' as the note, then open the Follow-Up Queue.
tasks.expected: WHS-1001 appears in the Pending stage with the note 'check sleep', joining WHS-1006, and the Pending count reads 2.

tasks.task: Start the survey, answer Section A's three questions (age group 30-44, ethnicity Hispanic, overall wellness 8), click Next, and in Section B choose Yes on the pregnancy question.
tasks.expected: Section B initially shows only the pregnancy question; choosing Yes reveals exactly two additional questions (number of pregnancies and most recent year).

tasks.task: With no screener filters set, open the export composer's preview.
tasks.expected: The preview shows one line per respondent — 8 lines — and the summary line reports 8 respondents with an average wellness of 6.7 / 10.

tasks.task: In the export composer, uncheck the ethnicity column checkbox.
tasks.expected: Ethnicity disappears from every preview line immediately, while the 8 lines and the summary stay intact.

tasks.task: Set the screener filters to the 60+ age group plus the Asian ethnicity, then look at the export preview.
tasks.expected: No respondent matches; the preview shows a friendly no-match note rather than a blank panel, and the summary reports 0 respondents without any NaN or broken average.

tasks.task: Open the export preview with default settings and read the first respondent line and the summary.
tasks.expected: IDs appear in the WHS-#### style and every wellness value carries one decimal with ' / 10', matching the app-wide formats.

tasks.task: In the insights strip, click the toggle to view just the two most recent weeks.
tasks.expected: The average wellness reads 7.0 / 10 for the recent window (Weeks 3 and 4: WHS-1005, WHS-1006, WHS-1007, WHS-1008) — different from the all-time 6.7 / 10.

tasks.task: Open the cohort screener page.
tasks.expected: Its page title is left-aligned with a short dark cyan underline bar, the respondent table has zebra striping on alternating rows, and primary action buttons are pill-shaped dark cyan with white text.

tasks.expected: Exactly three seeded flags (WHS-1006, WHS-1003, WHS-1004) sit on white cards with 12px rounded corners and a soft shadow, and each WHS ID renders as a light-cyan monospace chip.

tasks.task: Open the survey wizard.
tasks.expected: The Next button is pill-shaped dark cyan with white text, and the page title carries the left-aligned dark cyan underline treatment.

tasks.task: Visit the home page and then the cohort screener's insights strip.
tasks.expected: Both surfaces show the same treatment — left-aligned titles with dark cyan underline bars and white panels with 12px rounded corners and soft shadows — with neither left on the old styling.

tasks.task: Open the Question Bank page.
tasks.expected: The overall wellness question carries a v2 badge with a history entry showing its old wording 'How healthy do you feel overall?', while every other question shows v1.

tasks.task: In the Question Bank, edit the ethnicity question's text to 'Which ethnicity best describes you?' and save.
tasks.expected: The ethnicity question's badge becomes v2 — not v3, even though another question is already on v2 — the wellness question stays at v2, and a new changelog entry appears at the top of the history showing the before and after wording.

tasks.task: Edit any question in the Question Bank, clear its text completely, and try to save.
tasks.expected: Saving is rejected with an error message, and the question's wording and version badge remain unchanged.

tasks.expected: Section A of the wizard shows the new wording 'What is your age bracket?' on its age question immediately.

tasks.expected: The preview shows one line per respondent — 8 lines — and the summary line reports 8 respondents with an average wellness of 6.7 / 10.

tasks.task: Open the Program Outcomes page and read the follow-up rollup.
tasks.expected: The stage counts read Pending 1, Contacted 1, Resolved 1, and the resolution rate shows 33.3%.

tasks.task: On the Program Outcomes page, read the three steps of the outcome funnel.
tasks.expected: The funnel reads 3 flagged, then 2 reached Contacted or beyond, then 1 Resolved — WHS-1004's Resolved flag also counts in the middle step, so it shows 2, not the 1-1-1 a build counting only who currently sits in each stage would show.

tasks.task: On the Program Outcomes page, scroll to the suggested-flags section.
tasks.expected: It shows a friendly nobody-to-suggest note — WHS-1003 and WHS-1006, the only respondents under 6.0, are already flagged — rather than a blank area or a list repeating already-flagged respondents.

tasks.task: On the Follow-Up Queue, advance WHS-1003 to Resolved, then open the Program Outcomes page.
tasks.expected: Resolved now counts 2 and the resolution rate reads 66.7%, while the funnel's flagged step stays at 3 and its Resolved step now reads 2.
